subject: VM evidence handoff: scan cadence, SLAs, and CVE attestation
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintrust.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: vulnerability management cadence + SLA attestation

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor evidence collection for our Q4 audit we need a compact packet that shows Redwood's practical VM cadence and SLA commitments. Specifically FinTrust is asking for: 
- A one-page summary that states scan cadence (authenticated vs unauthenticated) and retention of scan results
- A table showing SLA/CVE remediation target windows (Critical/High/Medium/Low) and the expected timelines you commit to for our contract
- A recent remediation tracker that shows the last 90 days of critical/high CVE closures (CVE id, first seen, fix date, delta)
- A signed attestation page (PDF) stating the above and naming Redwood's SOC2 control IDs that map to the process if possible

Can you deliver this by COB Friday 2026-09-17 PST? If you can include hash or source for the scan file we can ingest it into our portal.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Wu
Security Operations Manager, FinTrust
security@fintrust.com

---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintrust.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: vulnerability management cadence + SLA attestation

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to provide a compact packet that matches everything on your list. High level notes up front: 
- Scan cadence: authenticated credentialed scans run weekly against prod services; unauthenticated scans run every 72 hours for external exposure. Results retained 12 months in our scan archive.
- Remediation SLAs (our standard customer commitments): Critical = 7 calendar days from triage, High = 30 days, Medium = 90 days, Low = 180 days. These are the values we will attest to in the attached PDF.
- Evidence: I'll attach a 2-page summary + a CSV export of the last 90 days with delta columns. I've pulled the tracker to show confirmed fix dates for critical/high items.

Plan/timeline: I will assemble the packet and upload signed attestation to DocuSign and share links by Fri 2026-09-17 16:00 PST. If FinTrust needs signed, notarized paperwork we can route to legal but that will add a day.

Attachments I will include: RI_VM_scan_summary_2026-09.pdf (includes cadence, retention, SOC2 refs), RI_cve_remediation_tracker_20260915.csv, RI_sla_attestation_sept2026.pdf (signed).

If you need a specific hash format for the PDF/CSV, let me know (SHA256 fine).

Thanks,
—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Wu <alice.wu@fintrust.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: vulnerability management cadence + SLA attestation

Stephanie — quick notes from a FinTrust intake: 
- They ask explicitly for authenticated scan receipts (proof an authenticated scan ran against host list). Please include scan job IDs and the credential type used (read-only service account).
- For the remediation tracker, mark whether fixes were code changes vs infra config changes vs dependency updates (column: remediation_type).
- On the attestation PDF, add a one-sentence linkage to SOC2 CC7 / CC8 (or whichever control IDs we map to VM). We should avoid overclaiming — simple mapping is fine.

I uploaded a scratch doc with a suggested template — use the "summary" doc folder: https://drive.redwood.dev/Shared/FinTrust/VM/2026-09/summary (linked)

If you want me to sign off before it goes out, ping me and I'll review.

-Lauren
Head of Trust & Safety (acting)
Redwood Inference

Alice / team — attached is the finalized packet per your request. Highlights below and attachment index: 

Attachment index:
- RI_VM_scan_summary_2026-09.pdf (2 pages) — lists credentialed scan cadence, unauthenticated cadence, retention policy, and SOC2 control mapping: CC7 (system monitoring) and CC8 (change management).
- RI_cve_remediation_tracker_20260915.csv — last 90 days; columns: cve_id, first_seen, fix_date, delta_days, remediation_type, notes, internal_scan_job_id
- RI_sla_attestation_sept2026.pdf — signed attestation from Redwood Security leadership committing to the stated SLAs for FinTrust's contract.

Proof items included in CSV: sample internal_scan_job_id values and a checksum column for the scan export we sent. Scan job IDs are internal run IDs; hashes for the PDF/CSV are SHA256: 
- RI_VM_scan_summary_2026-09.pdf: 3b7a1d9b5f2c3d6e9a2f4c4c3d1a9e77b8b6c5d4f3e2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d2
- RI_cve_remediation_tracker_20260915.csv: a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0

On SLA scope: these SLAs apply to vulnerabilities detected by our authenticated scans against customer-managed production environments and to third-party dependencies identified in our SBOM/scan pipeline. For vulnerabilities detected only by unauthenticated external scans, triage may differ; we still commit to the same remediation windows after triage.

If FinTrust needs a short call to walk through the tracker, I'm available Monday morning. If everything looks good I'll send the DocuSign link for the attestation so Alice can countersign.

Regards,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
